Al-Baghawi, *Ma'alim al-Tanzil*, on surah 31, verse 12:

Exalted is He. ﴿And We had already given Luqman wisdom﴾. He means: intellect, knowledge, acting upon it, and correctness in affairs.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: He was Luqman ibn Na'ur ibn Nahur ibn Tarikh, and he is Azar. Wahb said: He was the nephew (son of the sister) of Ayyub.[[See al-Bahr al-Muhit: 7/186.]] Muqatil said: It is mentioned that he was the cousin (son of the maternal aunt) of Ayyub.[[See al-Bahr al-Muhit: 7/186.]][[What is between the brackets is missing from manuscript "A".]] Al-Waqidi said: He was a judge among the Children of Israel.[[See al-Bahr al-Muhit: 7/186.]]

The scholars agreed that he was a sage (hakim), but was not a prophet (nabi), except for Ikrimah, who said: Luqman was a prophet. He stood alone in this view. Some of them said: Luqman was given the choice between prophethood and wisdom, and he chose wisdom.[[Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir (3/444): "The early scholars (al-salaf) differed over whether Luqman was a prophet or a righteous servant without prophethood, into two opinions. The majority hold the second (meaning he was not a prophet)." Then he cited some reports, some of which explicitly deny that he was a prophet, and some of which imply it. In some of them there is an indication that he was a servant who had been subjected to slavery. He said: Being a servant who had been subjected to slavery contradicts his being a prophet, because the messengers were sent from among the noble families of their peoples. He said: For this reason, the majority of the early scholars held that he was not a prophet. He said: The report that he was a prophet is transmitted from Ikrimah only if the chain of transmission to him is sound. He said: Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related it through the hadith of Waki' from Isra'il from Jabir from Ikrimah, who said: Luqman was a prophet. He said: This Jabir is Ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, and he is weak. And Allah knows best. Then Ibn Kathir said: What Sa'id ibn Abi 'Urwa related from Qatadah concerning the words of the Exalted, ﴿And We had already given Luqman wisdom﴾, means understanding of Islam, and he was not a prophet, and revelation did not come to him. End quote. This indicates that he was a righteous servant and not a prophet.]]

It is related that he was sleeping at midday when he was called: "O Luqman, would you like Allah to make you a successor (khalifah) on the earth, so that you may judge between the people with truth?" He answered the voice, saying: "If my Lord gives me the choice, I accept well-being and do not accept trial. If He makes it binding upon me, then it is hearing and obeying, for I know that if He does this to me, He will help me and protect me." The angels said, with a voice that they (the people) could not see: "Why, O Luqman?" He said: "Because the judge is in the most difficult and troubled of positions; injustice besets it from every place. If he is just, he is worthy of being saved, and if he errs, he errs off the path to Paradise. Whoever is humbled in this world is better than one who is noble (in it), and whoever chooses this world over the Hereafter, this world will tempt him and he will not attain the Hereafter." The angels marvelled at the goodness of his speech. So he slept a sleep, and he was given wisdom, and he woke up speaking it. Then Dawud was called after him, and he accepted it, and he did not stipulate what Luqman had stipulated, so he fell into sin more than once, and Allah pardoned him each time. Luqman used to support him with his wisdom.[[Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/510-511) to al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi in Nawadir al-Usul. Attributing it to him indicates weakness.]]

It is related from Khalid al-Raba'i, who said: Luqman was an Abyssinian servant, a carpenter.[[Related by al-Tabari: 21/67-68.]] Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: He was a tailor.[[Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/510) to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad in al-Zuhd, and Ibn al-Mundhir.]] It was also said: He was a shepherd. It is related that a man met him while he was speaking with wisdom, and said: "Are you not so-and-so the shepherd? By what did you attain what you have attained?" He said: "By truthfulness of speech, fulfilling trusts, and leaving what does not concern me."[[See: al-Tabari 21/68, and al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/512.]] Mujahid said: He was a black servant with large lips and cracked feet.[[Related by al-Tabari: 21/67.]]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿That give thanks to Allah. And whoever gives thanks, he gives thanks only for himself. And whoever is ungrateful, then indeed Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy.﴾

The others read it with tanwin (nun) in the singular form, and its meaning is also plural, as in His saying: ﴿And if you should count the favor of God, you could not enumerate it﴾ [Ibrahim: 14].

[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab: 8/419 with two weak chains.]] Al-Dahhak said: the outward is beauty of form and proportion of the limbs, and the inward is knowledge (ma'rifah). Muqatil said: the outward is the proportioning of creation, provision, and Islam, and the inward is what He has concealed of sins. [[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab: 8/418, and Ibn Abi al-Dunya in al-Shukr p. 109, with a weak chain.]] Al-Rabi' said: the outward is by the limbs, and the inward is by the heart. It was said: the outward is verbal affirmation by the tongue, and the inward is belief in the heart. It was said: the outward is the completeness of provision, and the inward is good character. 'Ata' said: the outward is the lightening of the laws (shara'i'), and the inward is intercession.

Mujahid said: the outward is the manifestation of Islam and victory over enemies, and the inward is reinforcement by the angels. It was said: the outward is reinforcement by the angels, and the inward is the casting of terror into the hearts of the disbelievers. Sahl ibn 'Abd Allah said: the outward is following the Messenger, and the inward is love for him.

﴿And among the people is one who disputes about God without knowledge﴾: it was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Ubayy ibn Khalaf, Umayya ibn Khalaf, and their likes, who used to dispute with the Prophet (ﷺ) about God and His attributes without knowledge. [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 6/351.]] ﴿Nor guidance, nor an illuminating Book﴾

﴿And whoever submits his face to Allah﴾ means: to Allah, that is, he sincerely devotes his religion to Allah and entrusts his affair to Allah, ﴿while he is a doer of good﴾ in his deed, ﴿then he has grasped the most reliable handhold﴾ meaning: he has held fast to the most trustworthy covenant, the one whose severance is not to be feared. ﴿And to Allah is the outcome of affairs.﴾

Indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.﴾ His statement, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And if whatever trees upon the earth were pens and the sea [were ink], replenished thereafter by seven seas, the words of Allah would not be exhausted.﴾ The verse [continues]. The exegetes said: it was revealed in Makkah, [along with] His statement, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿And they ask you about the soul.
